Definition: to occupy (by driving out previous tenants, and possessing in their place); by implication, to seize, to rob, to inherit; also to expel, to impoverish, to ruin
BiblicalUsage: Yârash is the word for possessing the land, for taking it and holding it as an inheritance. Caleb stilled the people and said, let us go up at once and possess it, and Moses set the land before Israel that they might go in and possess what God swore to their fathers. Joshua commanded the people to prepare, because within three days they would pass over Jordan to possess the land the LORD their God gave them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God gives the land before His people possess it, and the promise comes first and the possession follows. My position is that the inheritance is not taken by strength but received by faith, and Caleb's courage was simply believing God's word. And I hold that what God has given me in Christ is mine to possess now, not someday.
